ak-docs.tagline: Create, refresh, summarize, or audit evidence-based project docs.
ak-docs.summary: ak:docs reads the codebase and keeps the smallest doc set that explains purpose, contracts, evidence, and operations. Code owns WHAT/HOW; docs own WHY/WHERE, and the root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md holds agent behavior rules. Writing nothing is the correct result when no durable guidance is new, and the skill never writes product code.
howItWorks: Opening gate: a short brainstorm fixes readers (human, AI, or both), outcome, evidence sources, and acceptance criteria.
Reuses an accepted plan or brainstorm when one exists.
Routes on the first word: init, update, summarize, agent-context, agents, or llms, each with its own reference file.
Empty or ambiguous input triggers a question; it never defaults to init.
Discovery reads AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, README.md, the docs index, docs/, then source, tests, scripts, and live state.
An explicit route (repository instructions or --preset classic) overrides discovered file names.
Loads doc-content-rules.md for every write; loads operational-lookup.md when a route to an external system changes.
Operational route records cover when to use, scope, source of truth, lookup, access, limits, and fallback.
Route records store where to fetch a secret, never the secret value.
init inspects the project, designs the smallest route, has docs-manager write it, then validates links, paths, and commands.
update maps each changed claim to its owner and prunes: code restatements become pointers, WHY stays.
summarize returns an evidence-backed summary and writes a file only when the project or user asks.
agents mines git history and CI for recurring failures, ranks signals, distills DO/DON'T rules, and asks for diff approval.
llms updates llms.txt and llms-full.txt in place, following llmstxt.org grammar and keeping curated order.
Final check verifies every path, command, config key, and behavior claim, then reports created, changed, kept, and deleted files.
useWhen: Onboard a repo with no docs and set up a minimal doc route (init).
A merge changed contracts, paths, or ops routes like deploy paths and log sources (update).
You need an evidence-backed summary of the codebase or a topic without new files (summarize).
Write, audit, or tighten the root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (agent-context).
Distill DO/DON'T agent rules from repeated failures in git, CI, and source markers (agents).
Generate or refresh llms.txt/llms-full.txt (llms).
avoidWhen: Context for a subfolder, not the root: use ak-folder-context.
Content must come from the user's own decisions, not code: use ak-interview-docs.
You only need llms.txt with --url/--output and the generator script: use ak-llms.
You want a chronological session log: use ak-journal.
You need product code: use ak-cook; ak:docs never writes it.

params.name: init
params.desc: Set up a minimal, project-specific doc route. No empty placeholders, speculative roadmaps, or template-only ADRs; proposes the route before replacing existing docs.

params.name: update
params.desc: Reconcile affected docs with current evidence. Edits only affected surfaces, removes stale or duplicate content, adds no version notes or issue references.

params.name: summarize
params.desc: Summarize current evidence without forcing a new file; updates a summary file only when the project defines one or the user asks.

params.name: agent-context
params.desc: Write, audit, or optimize the root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md using a keep-or-cut filter and write/don't-write rules.

params.name: agents
params.desc: Mine bounded git and CI history for recurring failures and gotchas, then distill DO/DON'T rules into the root context file. Default window: 90 days or 300 commits (whichever is smaller) and 200 CI runs. Implies --advice and requires diff approval. Falls back to git-only if gh is not authenticated.

params.name: [bound]
params.desc: agents only: override the window with days (e.g. agents 30d) or a commit count (e.g. agents 500).

params.name: llms
params.desc: Generate or update both llms.txt and llms-full.txt per llmstxt.org. Writes to the site's public/static folder if one exists, else repo root; updates in place.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: Spawn kongming for keep/cut/restructure advice before writing. kongming only advises; the skill owns all edits. Works with every operation; already implied by agents.

params.name: --audit
params.desc: agent-context: kongming audits the current file, then the user decides keep/cut/fix one question at a time; only confirmed changes apply. agents: same one-rule-per-question pace at approval.

params.name: --dry-run
params.desc: agents only: stop after signal ranking, report signals and watchlist, spawn no advisor, write nothing.

params.name: --source
params.desc: agents only: add a read-only source-tree pass via ak:scout alongside git/CI. Source-only clusters need 2+ anchors plus a code/test guard or git/CI corroboration. Combines with --dry-run and --audit.

params.name: --preset classic
params.desc: init only: use the classic docs/ layout (project-overview-pdr.md, code-standards.md, codebase-summary.md, design-guidelines.md, deployment-guide.md, system-architecture.md, project-roadmap.md). Picks file names only; files without real content are skipped.

examples.note: New repo without docs; the skill designs the smallest route.
Team wants fixed file names across projects, or tooling reads fixed paths.
After a refactor renamed modules, clean docs that drifted from code.
Quick evidence-backed summary of the auth flow, no files written.
Trim a bloated CLAUDE.md, deciding keep/cut per item by interview.
Preview 30 days of recurring-failure signals without writing.
Distill DO/DON'T rules from git/CI plus source-tree markers.
Create or sync llms.txt and llms-full.txt with current docs.

tips: Always name the operation; without one the skill asks instead of running init.
Keep docs to WHY/WHERE; update turns code restatements and command lists into pointers.
No new durable guidance means no-op: no timestamp bumps, reorders, or cosmetic rewrites.
Keep the root context file to short policy plus a pointer to the operational guide; no runbooks, URLs, or account IDs.
agents needs gh auth status to pass for CI signals; otherwise it uses git only.
Evergreen docs carry no dates, issue IDs, or phase labels; mark plans, reports, and audits as stateful records.
When docs cover testing, init/update also load ak:test practice rules for cross-checking.
artifacts: Doc files under docs/ (discovered route or classic preset)
Docs index / navigation file (when there are several docs)
Operational route records in the project's operational guide

ak-docs-seeker.tagline: Look up current library and framework docs via context7.com llms.txt.
ak-docs-seeker.summary: ak:docs-seeker finds technical docs script-first: it classifies the query, builds a context7.com URL, fetches llms.txt, and suggests a parallel reading plan. Input is a library plus optional topic, or an official docs URL; output is relevant doc URLs and content. Without llms.txt it falls back to repository analysis with Repomix.
howItWorks: Given an exact official docs URL, reads it directly and checks the version matches.
Runs node scripts/detect-topic.js "<query>" to classify the query; returns JSON {topic, library, isTopicSpecific}.
Runs node scripts/fetch-docs.js "<query>" to build the context7.com URL and fetch llms.txt, falling back topic → general → error.
For many URLs, pipes llms.txt into analyze-llms-txt.js to rank URLs and suggest 1, 3, 7 agents, or a phased read.
Reads URLs with web fetch or parallel agents as suggested.
Last resort: clones the official GitHub repo to /tmp, packs it with Repomix, and reads README, docs/, examples/, and API.
useWhen: You need the latest API or features and model knowledge may be stale.
You have a focused question, e.g. 'how to use the shadcn date picker' (topic search, about 10-15 s).
You need broad coverage of a framework like Next.js for planning (library search, about 30-60 s).
The library is not on context7 and has no llms.txt.
avoidWhen: Generating llms.txt for your own project: use ak-llms or /ak:docs llms.
Comparing solutions, architectures, or best practices: use ak-research.
Packing the current repo as LLM context: use ak-repomix.
Questions about internal code, not an external library: use ak-scout.

params.name: [library-name]
params.desc: Library or framework to look up (e.g. next.js, shadcn); detect-topic.js extracts it from the query.

params.name: [topic]
params.desc: Specific topic in the library. With a topic: fast topic search (2-3 URLs). Without: general library search (8+ URLs).

examples.note: Topic query; quickly returns 2-3 relevant URLs.
Next.js overview; the script suggests how many agents read in parallel.
Check the latest API before implementing.
Niche library; may fall back to Repomix repo analysis.

tips: Optional keys in the skill's .env: CONTEXT7_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN (higher rate limits), GEMINI_API_KEY. Precedence: process.env > skill .env > plugin .env > project .env.
Scripts need Node; their output still costs context, so read only bounded output.
Pass the official docs URL if you know it to skip discovery.
Repo analysis is slow (5-10 min) and token-heavy; use it only without llms.txt.
Confirm the fetched docs match the library version your project uses (see references/advanced.md).
agents: Parallel reader agents as suggested by analyze-llms-txt.js (source names no specific subagent type)
artifacts: No fixed files; repo-analysis fallback clones into /tmp/docs-analysis and creates repomix-output.xml

ak-document-skills.tagline: Read, create, and edit Office files: docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx.
ak-document-skills.summary: ak:document-skills routes by format to Word (ak:docx), PDF (ak:pdf), PowerPoint (ak:pptx), or spreadsheet (ak:xlsx) workflows. Input is format, file path, and action; output is an extracted, created, or edited file that has been validated. It preserves templates and existing content, and runs and validates each workflow instead of stopping at routing.
howItWorks: Detects the target format and loads the matching child skill: ak-docx, ak-pdf, ak-pptx, or ak-xlsx.
docx: extract, create (docx-js.md), edit (ooxml.md), or redline others' documents (redline.md); keeps runs, comments, and tracked changes, then validates and renders.
pdf: extract text/tables, create, merge/split/rotate, fill forms, OCR/watermark; checks page count, order, and fillable fields.
pptx: create (html2pptx.md), use a template, edit (ooxml.md), or extract; keeps masters, notes, and relationships; checks each slide for overlap, clipping, and contrast.
xlsx: pandas for data, openpyxl for formulas and formatting; uses Excel formulas, not hardcoded values.
xlsx: runs python recalc.py output.xlsx to recalculate and fix #REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #NAME?.
Multi-format requests run each workflow and validate each file; missing renderers are reported, not faked.
useWhen: Create a Word report, edit a contract with tracked changes, or extract text from .docx.
Extract tables from a PDF, merge/split PDFs, or fill PDF forms.
Build a .pptx deck from content or edit one on a company template.
Analyze data or build a spreadsheet with formulas, charts, or pivots in .xlsx/.csv.
avoidWhen: Just reading long markdown in a browser: use ak-markdown-novel-viewer.
You need an HTML presentation page: use ak-show-off or ak-preview.
Pure image OCR/vision the model can't handle: consider ak-ai-multimodal.

params.name: <docx|pdf|pptx|xlsx>
params.desc: Required: format to process; selects the child skill (ak:docx, ak:pdf, ak:pptx, ak:xlsx).

params.name: [path]
params.desc: Input or output file path.

params.name: [action]
params.desc: Per child skill: docx/pptx use create|edit|extract; pdf uses extract|create|merge|split|fill; xlsx uses create|edit|analyze.

examples.note: Edit a contract, keep formatting, and track changes.
Extract figure tables from PDF invoices.
Fill a PDF form while keeping fields fillable.
Create a new deck without a template.
Analyze sales data and add summary formulas.

tips: openpyxl writes formula text but not values; run recalc.py (needs an engine such as LibreOffice) or cells open empty.
Empty extraction from a scanned PDF does not mean no content; use OCR or inspect visually.
For legal or business documents from others, use the redline workflow for precise tracked changes.
Render and check layout after editing pptx/docx; without a renderer the skill reports it as unverified.
Leave master slides, styles, notes, and relationships untouched unless asked.
artifacts: Rendered layout-check images (when a renderer is available)

ak-folder-context.tagline: Create a compact subfolder CLAUDE.md plus linked AGENTS.md for local conventions.
ak-folder-context.summary: ak:folder-context writes durable context for one subfolder: decisions, conventions, or ongoing work a future agent can't infer. Input is the target folder; output is a compact CLAUDE.md there and an AGENTS.md symlink to it. It never touches the root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and refuses static reference folders.
howItWorks: Confirms the target is a subfolder, not the root, and reads key local source, config, and Markdown.
Sanity gate: skips static reference folders and folders whose context is easy to discover on demand.
On an explicit request, drafts the file in place for review; asks only on conflict with user content or overwrite.
Writes CLAUDE.md only from folder evidence or explicit user decisions, dropping empty sections.
Inherits root policy without repeating it; links to the operational guide instead of holding ops routes.
Creates AGENTS.md as a symlink to CLAUDE.md, or a one-line pointer file if symlinks fail.
Rereads user edits and flags contradictions, but never reverts them unless asked.
useWhen: A monorepo package has its own conventions (naming, MUST NOTs) that differ from root.
A folder has dated, locked decisions the next session must know.
Long-running work in one module needs context across sessions.
You want agents to follow local constraints without bloating the root CLAUDE.md.
avoidWhen: Editing the root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md: use /ak:docs agent-context.
Project docs under docs/: use ak-docs.
The folder holds only static reference material or easily discovered context.
Recording session history: use ak-journal.

params.name: <target-folder>
params.desc: Required: subfolder to create context for. Must not be the project root; the skill writes only inside the confirmed target.

examples.note: Billing package with its own currency-handling constraints.
Record the MUST NOT refactor rule for legacy code and why.
Mobile app in a monorepo with different build and naming conventions.

tips: Useful sections: purpose and key files (one line each), constraints (especially MUST NOTs), naming, dated decisions, cross-session context.
Use bullets; no directory trees or copies of general project docs.
Don't repeat root rules, invent constraints, store credentials, or write outside the target folder.
Keep deploy, log, and secret lookups out; link to the operational guide instead.
Respect existing local user instructions before adding new context.
Where symlinks aren't supported (e.g. Windows without permission), AGENTS.md is a one-line pointer file.

ak-interview-docs.tagline: Guided interview that turns the user's vision and decisions into durable docs.
ak-interview-docs.summary: ak:interview-docs turns the user's own knowledge, taste, and decisions into a README, ADR, strategy, principles, or other structured doc. Input is a vision, doc path, or topic; the doc is patched after every answer. It never invents content, ranks the user's lists on its own, or derives docs from source code.
howItWorks: Picks a mode: vision mode (project vision, README direction, ADR decisions) or structured-doc mode (principles, strategy, review, framework); asks once if both fit.
Vision mode reads README.md and docs navigation to find the existing owner of vision and decisions; it does not assume docs/adr exists.
Vision mode asks focused questions on open decisions, skipping answered ones, and patches the owner doc after each answer.
README keeps only vision; confirmed decisions go to the repo's chosen owner; ADRs only if already a convention.
Structured-doc mode reads nearby docs, creates a minimal skeleton once, then asks one concrete open question per turn.
Treats user lists as unordered until the user sets priority; keeps the user's wording and edits.
useWhen: Write a README that states the project vision in the founder's words.
Record architecture decisions the user already made as ADRs (if the repo uses ADRs).
Draft principles, strategy, or a personal framework one question at a time.
The user has ideas in mind but no structure to write them down.
avoidWhen: You want AI to propose and compare options: use ak-brainstorm.
The doc should be derived from code: use ak-docs.
You need a research brief for someone else: use ak-research-prompt.
You want a chronological technical log: use ak-journal.

params.name: <vision | document-path | topic>
params.desc: Required: a vision statement (vision mode), a doc path to build or finish, or a structured-doc topic (structured-doc mode).

examples.note: Vision mode: interview to write a direction-setting README.
Structured-doc mode: build a principles doc one question at a time.
Draft a strategy doc from the user's decisions.

examples.cmd: /ak:interview-docs decision to choose PostgreSQL over MongoDB
examples.note: Record a settled decision in the repo's decision owner.

tips: Tentative opinions never become decisions; ADRs hold only explicitly settled choices.
You can set an interview pace (e.g. one question at a time) and the skill keeps it.
The doc is patched after each answer, so you can stop midway without losing content.
It won't overwrite existing docs, add speculative sections, or store secrets or personal data.

ak-llms.tagline: Generate llms.txt (and llms-full.txt) per llmstxt.org from docs or a URL.
ak-llms.summary: ak:llms builds an LLM-friendly Markdown index of project docs following the llmstxt.org spec. Input is a docs path or URL (default: discovered from README, site config, and navigation); output is llms.txt and optionally llms-full.txt with inline content. It does not handle hosting, deploy, SEO, robots.txt, or sitemaps.
howItWorks: Gather: reads README and docs/site navigation to build an allowlist of public sources; for a URL, uses web search to get the structure.
Analyze: takes titles from navigation, frontmatter, or H1; summarizes real page content; groups pages (API, Guides, Reference) as core or optional.
Generate: runs scripts/generate-llms-txt.py --source <path> --output <output-path> --base-url <url> [--full], or writes by hand per the spec.
Structure: H1 project name, summary blockquote, H2 sections of [Title](url): description links, ## Optional last.
Validate: H1 and blockquote present, valid Markdown links, Optional last, short jargon-free descriptions.
useWhen: You publish a docs site and want AI tools to find it easily.
You need a compact context file for AI assistants reading project docs.
The user asks for 'llms.txt', 'LLM documentation', or 'AI-friendly docs'.
You need llms-full.txt with all content inline for one-shot loading.
avoidWhen: Updating llms.txt as part of the general docs workflow (discovery, in-place update of both files): use /ak:docs llms.
Looking up external library docs via llms.txt: use ak-docs-seeker.
The docs site runs on Mintlify and needs its AI features configured: use ak-mintlify.

params.name: [path|url]
params.desc: Folder/file to scan or docs site URL. Omitted: discovered from root README, site config, and navigation.

params.name: --full
params.desc: Also generate llms-full.txt with inline doc content.

params.name: --output path
params.desc: Custom output location; default is project root.

params.name: --url base
params.desc: Base URL prefix for links (e.g. https://example.com/docs); maps to the script's --base-url. Listed under Arguments though not in argument-hint.

examples.note: Discover project docs and write llms.txt at root.
Scan docs/ and also write llms-full.txt.
Write to the site's public folder with absolute links.
Build llms.txt from an existing docs site's structure.

tips: ## Optional must come last; agents may skip it on short context, so put changelogs and legacy there.
Don't copy a page's first paragraph as its description; it may be boilerplate. Summarize real content.
Exclude secrets, private docs, and unrelated config from public output.
generate-llms-txt.py needs Python; write by hand per the spec if the script doesn't fit.

ak-markdown-novel-viewer.tagline: Read markdown in a calm, book-like viewer served over local HTTP.
ak-markdown-novel-viewer.summary: ak:markdown-novel-viewer serves a Markdown file or folder from a local Node server with a book-style reader: novel theme, dark mode, progress bar, auto-hiding header. Input is a file or folder path; output is a localhost URL. Use it for long content such as RFCs, runbooks, design docs, reports, plans, or novels; HTML generation belongs to ak:preview --html.
howItWorks: Resolves and quotes the path, including Windows paths with spaces.
Reuses a known server for the project; checks processes and ports before starting a new one.
Checks Node and the marked, highlight.js, and gray-matter deps; runs npm install in the skill folder only if missing.
Runs node scripts/server.cjs --file "<absolute-path>" --open (or --dir), binds to localhost unless remote access is asked, and returns the real printed URL.
Records PID, port, and project; stops only its own server when done (--stop kills all viewer servers).
useWhen: Read a long RFC, design doc, or report without distractions.
Browse a multi-phase plan with a status sidebar and Previous/Next navigation.
Read docs with Mermaid diagrams, rendered to match the theme.
Browse a whole markdown folder with the directory browser.
avoidWhen: Generating an HTML explainer or slides: use ak-preview (--html).
A public showcase page: use ak-show-off.
A kanban plan dashboard: use ak-plans-kanban.
Reading a few lines in the terminal; no server needed.

params.name: [file-or-directory]
params.desc: Markdown file (maps to --file) or folder (maps to --dir) to open.

params.name: --file <path>
params.desc: scripts/server.cjs option: markdown file to view.

params.name: --dir <path>
params.desc: CLI option: folder to browse.

params.name: --port <number>
params.desc: CLI option: server port, default 3456.

params.name: --host <addr>
params.desc: CLI option: bind host, default localhost; 0.0.0.0 for remote access (only when asked).

params.name: --open
params.desc: CLI option: open the browser automatically, default false.

params.name: --background
params.desc: CLI option: run in the background, default false.

params.name: --stop
params.desc: CLI option: stops ALL viewer servers. Use only if every server belongs to this task; otherwise stop the specific PID.

examples.note: Read a long RFC in the browser.
Browse a multi-phase plan with sidebar and navigation.
Browse a folder of novel chapters.

tips: Shortcuts: ? cheatsheet, T theme, S sidebar, ←/→ switch phase, Esc close.
Always use the URL the server prints; it may not be port 3456.
Check processes and ports first to avoid duplicate servers; stop yours when done.
Mermaid errors usually come from bad syntax (e.g. -> instead of -->); see references/mermaid-diagrams.md.
artifacts: No doc files; starts a local Node server process (track its PID and port)

ak-mintlify.tagline: Build and maintain Mintlify docs: docs.json, MDX, navigation, OpenAPI, AI assets.
ak-mintlify.summary: ak:mintlify builds and maintains Mintlify docs sites that turn Markdown/MDX into interactive docs. Input is a task (config, content, navigation, OpenAPI, deploy, AI) and a docs root; output is edited docs.json, MDX pages, and navigation/theme config with validation run. It uses the installed CLI and version-matched official docs, and never installs a global CLI or inits a site just to edit MDX.
howItWorks: Inspects the docs root, package manifest, lockfile, config, and navigation before choosing commands.
Checks the installed CLI version and help, and uses matching official docs for config or API changes.
Routes by change: config/theme, content, navigation, OpenAPI, preview/deploy, or AI, each to its own reference file.
Loads quick-examples.md only when starting new content or config.
Runs installed validators (e.g. mint validate, mint broken-links, mint a11y, mint openapi-check) and checks affected links and rendering.
Reuses a running preview, tracks any process it starts, and stops it when done.
Deploys only to a requested target, with proof of the real result.
useWhen: Add a new MDX page using Mintlify components (Card, Tabs, Steps).
Reorganize navigation, tabs, or groups in docs.json.
Integrate OpenAPI/AsyncAPI to generate API reference pages.
Configure AI features such as llms.txt, skill.md, or MCP for the docs site.
Set up CI checks for broken links and a11y before deploy.
avoidWhen: The project doesn't use Mintlify and only needs in-repo markdown docs: use ak-docs.
You need a standalone llms.txt unrelated to Mintlify: use ak-llms.
Deploying an app to general hosting: use ak-deploy.
ASP.NET API docs: use dotnet-claude-kit:openapi or scalar.

params.name: [task]
params.desc: Work to do (config/theme, content, navigation, OpenAPI, preview/deploy, AI integration); decides which reference loads.

params.name: [path]
params.desc: Docs root or file to edit.

examples.note: Write a new MDX page and add it to navigation.
Generate API reference from an OpenAPI file.

examples.cmd: /ak:mintlify change theme and brand colors docs/docs.json
examples.note: Edit theme config in docs.json.
Run local validation before merging.

tips: Don't install a global CLI or run init just to edit one MDX file; use the project's CLI.
Checks in the references: mint validate, mint broken-links, mint a11y, mint openapi-check; MINTLIFY_CONFIG selects a docs.json per environment.
Mintlify auto-deploys from the connected Git repo; other targets (Vercel, AWS) need a static build and proof of result.
Stop any mint dev process you started so it doesn't hold the port.

ak-diagram.tagline: Compile typed JSON IR into validated SVG, fragments, or interactive HTML readers.
ak-diagram.summary: ak:diagram (v3) compiles a typed JSON IR into deterministic SVG, an embeddable HTML fragment, or a self-contained interactive HTML reader, fully offline. The compiler handles layout: ranking, column ordering, orthogonal edge routing, and role-based cards with a legend, so you describe topology and never enter coordinates. It supports 5 archetypes, 4 visual presets, and light/dark themes; the reader only queries nodes and relations declared in the IR.
howItWorks: Pick an archetype: architecture (components, boundaries, connections), workflow (lanes, steps, transitions), sequence (participants, messages), dataflow (stages, nodes, flows), or lifecycle (states, transitions).
Write the IR envelope {"schema_version": 1, "diagram_type": "<type>", "meta": {...}}, choose preset and theme, optionally "trace" animation and up to 5 meta.views chapters.
Schema rules: strict role enum on nodes (checked at compile) and IDs matching ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$.
Placement comes from the IR: layer sets architecture columns, lane sets workflow rows, stage.order sets dataflow columns, initial state starts lifecycles.
Unranked nodes take the longest path from predecessors; cycles render as return routes.
Compile offline: node scripts/compiler/compile.mjs --input diagram.json --format html|svg|fragment --out <path> --preset <preset> --theme <theme>.
python3 scripts/render.py auto-detects IR, Mermaid, or legacy templates.
Deterministic: same IR gives same geometry and same SHA-256 output; no overlaps, no routes through unrelated nodes (tested on every fixture).
Each role maps to a visual family (client, service, data, queue, gateway, and more) with its own color, sigil, and legend entry.
Motion is CSS-only, staggered by column, under 8 seconds total; prefers-reduced-motion shows the final frame.
Delivers .html (reader with search, focus, routes, role lens, chapters, share card, theme toggle, replay) or clean .svg.
useWhen: Microservice architecture with boundaries and layers, as an interactive reader for search, focus, and tracing.
Multi-lane workflows with handoffs and decision points, without hand-placing coordinates.
API call sequences or ETL/stream/data-lineage pipelines (dataflow).
An order-status state machine (lifecycle) with storytelling chapters via meta.views.
Deterministic output (same IR, same SHA-256) to commit and diff in review.
avoidWhen: Freeform, editable whiteboard sketches: use ak-excalidraw.
Static publication-grade diagrams or print infographics: use ak-tech-graph.
Inline diagrams in markdown: use ak-mermaidjs-v11.
Slides or a broad visual explanation instead of a system map: use ak-preview.

params.name: [input-file]
params.desc: Typed JSON IR file (compile.mjs --input). The render.py wrapper also takes Mermaid .mmd (vendored v11.4.1) or legacy templates.

params.name: --format <svg|fragment|html>
params.desc: svg: clean vector (keeps CSS animation). fragment: scoped HTML for an existing page. html: self-contained interactive reader with shortcuts.

params.name: --preset <classic|signal-flow|blueprint|editorial>
params.desc: Visual preset; changes typography, strokes, and density, not graph meaning. classic (default, neutral), signal-flow (emerald/cyan glow), blueprint (technical grid, monospace), editorial (warm serif).

params.name: --theme <light|dark>
params.desc: Light or dark theme; the reader has a toggle that keeps geometry and preset.

ak-excalidraw.tagline: Draw reasoning Excalidraw diagrams via live MCP canvas or Playwright-rendered files.
ak-excalidraw.summary: ak:excalidraw makes editable Excalidraw diagrams for architecture, data flow, workflows, and system design. Shapes should carry meaning, not just be labeled boxes. Mode A uses a live MCP canvas (preferred); Mode B writes a .excalidraw file and renders PNG with Playwright. Input is a description or path (including 'diagram this repo'); output is a .excalidraw file plus PNG/SVG.
howItWorks: Mode detection: uses Mode A if mcp__excalidraw__read_diagram_guide is available and works, else Mode B file-based; guides setup if neither works.
Assess depth: simple concept or full technical diagram; technical ones need real specs, events, and APIs as evidence.
Map concepts to visual patterns (fan-out, convergence, tree, timeline, cycle, assembly line, side-by-side, gap), varying patterns per major concept.
Plan layout left→right or top→bottom, giving important parts more whitespace.
Repo auto-diagram: detect, discover components (≤15 tool calls), map connections (≤10), verify, then generate (max 12 components, 20 arrows).
Self-critique loop: render, compare with the design, fix overlap, clipped text, and wrong arrows (usually 2-4 rounds, max 2 with MCP).
Export on request: MCP uses export_to_image (PNG/SVG); file mode runs render_excalidraw.py for PNG.
useWhen: The user says 'diagram this repo' or 'visualize the architecture'.
You need a diagram that stays editable in Excalidraw.
Explain a concept or mental model with a diagram that argues visually.
Draw data flow or system design live on a canvas with the user.
avoidWhen: Validated system maps from JSON IR with an interactive reader: use ak-diagram.
Static publication-grade diagrams with fixed styles: use ak-tech-graph.
Inline diagrams in markdown: use ak-mermaidjs-v11.
Slides or page-style visual explanations: use ak-preview.

The most common flaw is cramped spacing: boxes 200-240px, labeled arrow gaps 150-200px, rows 280-350px.
Keep under 30% of text inside containers; use 3-4 fill colors max; same role, same color (Frontend #a5d8ff, Backend #d0bfff, Database #b2f2bb).
When editing an existing diagram, keep element IDs, bindings, palette, and fonts.
With MCP, clear the canvas and screenshot to confirm it's empty before drawing.

ak-mermaidjs-v11.tagline: Write Mermaid.js v11 diagrams: flowchart, sequence, class, ER, Gantt, state, and more.
ak-mermaidjs-v11.summary: ak:mermaidjs-v11 writes text diagrams in Mermaid.js v11 declarative syntax, covering 24+ diagram types. Input is a diagram type or description; output is a mermaid code block for inline Markdown, or SVG/PNG/PDF via mermaid-cli when needed. It is the lightest option for diagrams in docs, READMEs, and PRs.
howItWorks: Picks a diagram type (flowchart, sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, stateDiagram, erDiagram, gantt, journey; see references/diagram-types.md).
Writes {diagram-type} plus content, with optional frontmatter config (theme, look) and %% comments.
For Markdown hosts, outputs a mermaid code block with no CLI; checks host support for less common v11 features.
Exports only when needed with mmdc (@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli): -i/-o, -t theme, -b background, --cssFile; checks the result.
Customizes via configuration.md (theme, look, fontFamily, securityLevel) or embeds via the JavaScript API (integration.md).
useWhen: Add inline diagrams to a README, docs, or PR description.
Draw an ER diagram for a database schema.
Build a Gantt timeline or user journey.
Draw a sequence diagram of an API flow in docs.
avoidWhen: Validated interactive system maps: use ak-diagram.
Publication-grade diagrams in multiple styles: use ak-tech-graph.
Freeform editable canvas: use ak-excalidraw.
Complex data charts: use the dataviz skill.

ak-tech-graph.tagline: Generate publication-grade SVG+PNG technical diagrams in 7 visual styles.
ak-tech-graph.summary: ak:tech-graph creates technical diagrams as SVG and exports PNG via rsvg-convert: architecture, data flow, flowchart, sequence, agent/memory, concept map, UML, ER, network topology, and more. Styles: Flat Icon (default), Dark Terminal, Blueprint, Notion Clean, Glassmorphism, Claude Official, OpenAI Official. Input is a diagram type or system description; output is a .svg and .png pair for publishing.
howItWorks: Recovers entities, edges, and claims from source evidence or the user's description; flags uncertain relations.
Keeps any supplied style or brand, else defaults to Flat Icon; loads the style reference and diagram-type-layout-rules.md.
Builds SVG with a helper (generate-from-template.py from template + JSON) or by hand per drawing-recipes.md; keeps arrow meaning and readable labels.
Validates and exports with generate-diagram.sh (or validate-svg.sh plus rsvg-convert -w 1920).
Inspects the export for collisions, clipped text, and wrong relations, then fixes and re-exports; reports quality as unverified if it can't view images.
Returns SVG and PNG paths with the real validation status.
useWhen: Polished architecture diagrams for blogs, articles, or slides.
Illustrate a RAG pipeline, agentic search, multi-agent system, or memory layer.
Diagrams in Anthropic or OpenAI house style.
Both SVG and retina PNG (1920px) for publishing.
avoidWhen: Inline diagrams in markdown docs: use ak-mermaidjs-v11.
Interactive HTML readers from JSON IR: use ak-diagram.
Editable canvas: use ak-excalidraw.
Quick visual self-review only: use /ak:preview --diagram.

ak-show-off.tagline: Build self-contained HTML showcase pages with section screenshots and optional publishing.
ak-show-off.summary: ak:show-off builds a self-contained, responsive HTML showcase with a striking hero and smooth-scrolling sections for demos, social posts, or article images. Input is markdown or a prompt; output is content.md, the HTML page, per-section screenshots in landscape/portrait/square, and an optional agentwiki publish. It remembers user preferences (screenshots, publishing, languages) and builds with ak:frontend-design and ak:diagram.
howItWorks: Resolves preferences with node scripts/preferences.js get (defaults: screenshots=true, publishing=true, languages=[vi,en]).
Detects intent to turn off screenshots or publishing, change language, or reset; saves it unless the user says 'just this once'.
For multi-artifact or publish work, creates or reuses a plan via project-management with a checklist.
Splits the request into 2-6 sections (including hero), fact-checks online, and writes assets/showoff/<mission-name>/content.md with citations.
Publishes the document with the agentwiki CLI when publishing=true.
Builds HTML with ak:frontend-design first, then ak:diagram for system maps, falling back to inline SVG; adds parallax and a system/light/dark toggle.
Editorial visuals: AntV Infographic for KPI/list/quadrant panels (3+ tiles), diagram-design for section diagrams; each can be turned off by flag.
With screenshots=true, runs node scripts/capture-sections.js; the rws screenshot API fallback needs publishing=true, RWEB_API_KEY, and public HTML.
Runs a 5-point handoff gate (context fit, hierarchy, craft, usability/a11y, safety), publishes if enabled, and opens the page.
useWhen: Show off a finished feature or project with a polished HTML page.
You need section images at 16:9, 9:16, and 1:1 for social media.
Build a bilingual Vietnamese-English showcase with cited sources.
Turn a markdown file into an interactive showcase with diagrams.
avoidWhen: Explaining code or architecture, or internal slides: use ak-preview.
Real product UI: use ak-frontend-design.
Just reading long markdown: use ak-markdown-novel-viewer.

ak-copywriting.tagline: Conversion copy: formulas, headlines, emails, landing pages, CTAs, style extraction.
ak-copywriting.summary: Writes high-converting copy from an agreed deliverable, audience, goal, and brand voice. Ships a formula library (AIDA, PAS, BAB, 4Ps, FAB), headline/email/landing/CTA templates, power words, and 30 writing styles, plus a script that extracts a style from sample files.
howItWorks: Identify deliverable, audience, goal, and brand voice from the brief; ask only when a missing choice changes the copy.
Load the matching references: landing/CTA, email, headlines, social, or style extraction.
Use formulas as optional structure; voice wins (no fake urgency for a calm brand).
Tie every product claim, number, or testimonial to evidence; never invent social proof.
Deliver in the requested format and path; check audience fit, claim support, and CTA.
useWhen: Headlines, landing pages, CTAs, or emails that must convert.
Applying a custom writing style stored in assets/writing-styles/.
Generating copy variants for an A/B test.
avoidWhen: Technical docs for developers or CLAUDE.md: use ak-docs.
An HTML demo page showcasing the product: use ak-show-off.
